title: FACT CHECK: Marcos did not tell Filipinos to ‘bathe once a week’ to save water
summary: The fake quote card twists the President’s October 11 statement urging households to collect rainwater in preparation for Super El Niño

blocks.text: Claim: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told Filipinos to conserve water by bathing only once a week and share one bucket of water among 10 people.

Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Madz Jenn shared a post on November 7 showing Marcos at a podium bearing the presidential seal. The post bears a quote attributed to the President: “Mag praktis na kayong isang beses lang maligo sa isang linggo para tipid sa tubig… pagkasyahin ang isang baldeng tubig sa 10 katao.”
(Practice bathing just once a week to save water… make do with one bucket of water for 10 people.)
As of writing, the post has 1,200 reactions, 269 comments, and 617 shares.
Some users who interacted with the post believed it to be true. One user commented: “Bwisit talaga to, pati pag-ligo pakikialaman… Akala mo naman siya nagbabayad ng [tubig] namin.”
(This is really annoying, he’s even meddling with how we take a bath. You would think he’s paying our water bill.)

The facts: The quote is falsely attributed to Marcos. No credible news report, Presidential Communications Office release, or official video shows him making the statement depicted in the viral quote card.

The fake statement appears to build on Marcos’ remarks during an interview in Singapore on October 11. Discussing how households could prepare for possible water shortages due to the looming Super El Niño, he said: “Bumili na kayo ng balde para ‘pag umulan, makolekta na ninyo lahat.”
(Buy buckets now so that you can collect all the rainwater when it rains.)
He added that the government would provide water filters and teach the public how to use them properly.

The remark drew criticism online. On October 13, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro defended Marcos’ remarks, saying the President’s advice was serious and part of the government’s efforts to mitigate the effects of El Niño.
A day later, the Department of Social Welfare and Development demonstrated the water filtration kits it planned to distribute to communities vulnerable to El Niño.

Super El Niño: The fake quote card spread as the country braces for a severe dry spell. On November 5, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration announced that a very strong El Niño is now present in the tropical Pacific Ocean.

The weather bureau said it may peak by the end of 2026 but persist until the first half of 2027. Virtually the entire country could face drought by March 2027. (READ: FAST FACTS: What is a Super El Niño, and what should we expect from it?)

Malacañang has urged the public not to panic. On October 1, Castro asked households to fix leaks and cut unnecessary water use. She also warned that stockpiling potable water could create artificial shortages and drive up prices.
Marcos has also directed government agencies to take necessary measures to prepare for the impacts of the weather phenomenon, including allocating P7.7 billion for its El Niño response.

Other fact-checks: Rappler earlier debunked an AI-generated video supposedly showing people panic-buying water drums after the President’s October 11 remarks. The video garnered over 20 million views.
